e: RDS Proxy pools and multiplexes database connections, absorbing the unpredictable connection bursts from serverless applications so the DB instance doesn't reject connections, with little operational effort. Caching, a larger instance class, or Multi-AZ don't fix connection exhaustion.

Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks pause instances in the launch and terminate transitions so a custom script can send the audit report before the instance enters service or is terminated. Scheduled scripts or user data can't reliably cover termination.

A Network Load Balancer supports UDP traffic for the game servers, and DynamoDB on-demand scales automatically with no intervention for non-relational score data. ALBs don't support UDP, and Route 53 alone doesn't distribute UDP traffic to healthy Auto Scaling instances the same way.

Provisioned concurrency keeps Lambda execution environments initialized (libraries loaded), which removes cold-start latency, with the fewest operational changes. Bypassing the API, caching in S3, or enlarging the database don't address initialization latency.

A Lambda function that starts and stops the EC2 and RDS instances, invoked on a schedule by EventBridge, is serverless, cheap, and needs almost no maintenance. EC2 elastic resize and DB scale-to-zero don't exist this way, and an extra EC2 instance or Marketplace products add cost and upkeep.

Aurora PostgreSQL is compatible with PostgreSQL (minimal code change) and an Aurora Replica (a reader endpoint) can run the long reporting queries without affecting writes on the primary. In RDS Multi-AZ the standby can't serve queries, and DocumentDB or DynamoDB would require large code changes.
A TLS listener with a server certificate on the NLB encrypts traffic in transit between clients and the load balancer. Shield and WAF protect against attacks, and EBS encryption is for data at rest.

Licensing by sockets and cores, with licenses the company already owns, requires a Dedicated Host, and since the capacity and uptime are predictable, a Dedicated Host Reservation (1- or 3-year) is the most cost-effective choice. On-Demand Hosts cost more, and Dedicated Instances can't use socket/core licensing.

EFS is POSIX-compliant, shareable across EC2 instances in multiple AZs, highly durable, and its Standard class with a lifecycle policy to EFS Standard-IA lowers the cost of infrequently accessed data. S3 isn't POSIX-compliant, and One Zone classes store data in one AZ, reducing durability and availability.

Least privilege chains security groups: web servers accept HTTPS only from the load balancer's security group, and the MySQL servers accept port 3306 only from the web servers' security group. Allowing 0.0.0.0/0 is too broad, and network ACLs can't reference security groups.

ElastiCache caches frequently requested identical datasets in memory, reducing the number of database calls and improving backend performance. SNS and Kinesis Data Firehose aren't caches, and a read replica doesn't act as a cache of repeated results.

Following least privilege, give the engineer an IAM user in a group limited to CloudFormation actions, and have CloudFormation use a service role with permissions specific to the stack's resources, so the engineer can't exceed them. Root credentials, Administrator, or PowerUser are too broad.

Security groups deny inbound traffic by default, so the RDS instance's security group needs an inbound rule allowing MySQL traffic from the web tier's security group. Default network ACLs already allow all traffic, and routes within a VPC already exist (local route).

RDS read replicas serve the reporting queries using replicated data, so the primary handles writes without being affected. Multi-AZ standbys can't serve queries, and a load balancer or bigger instance doesn't isolate the workloads.

Session data must be stored durably outside the web servers: DynamoDB is a durable, scalable key-value store for sessions, and ElastiCache for Redis is an in-memory store with persistence and replication options suited to sessions. Sticky sessions are tied to an instance and aren't durable, and Cognito and Systems Manager Application Manager aren't session stores.

The web tier is stateless with no local storage, so just keeping the latest AMIs is enough (no EBS snapshots needed), and RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery meet the 2-hour RPO for the database while optimizing resource utilization.

Customers have dynamic IP addresses, so the web servers must allow HTTPS from anywhere (0.0.0.0/0), while the database should accept MySQL traffic only from the web servers' security group, never from the internet.

Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text and has built-in PII redaction, and a Lambda function triggered by the S3 upload starts the job and stores the output in a separate bucket. Textract reads documents, not audio, and the other options rely on custom PII scanning.

gp3 volumes max out at 16,000 IOPS, so degradation at 20,000 IOPS points to the volume limit. Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) provides much higher IOPS (up to 64,000 and more with Block Express). Magnetic is slower, and splitting the gp3 volume isn't possible for RDS.

AWS CloudTrail records API calls, including which IAM user changed the security group rules and when. Config shows what changed in a resource's configuration over time but CloudTrail identifies who did it; GuardDuty and Inspector don't track user changes.

AWS Shield Advanced can protect Global Accelerator accelerators, providing DDoS protection for the self-managed DNS service (UDP traffic) at the accelerator. WAF doesn't work for DNS/UDP traffic on accelerators or EC2 instances.

The job can run up to an hour with objects up to 10 GB, which exceeds Lambda's 15-minute limit. A Fargate ECS task launched by an EventBridge schedule runs the container serverlessly with no servers to manage. EC2 launch type needs instance management.

600 TB in 2 weeks over 100 Mbps isn't feasible (it would take years), and Direct Connect takes weeks to provision. Several Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices ship the data physically, encrypted, and are the most cost-effective option.

A Regional AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule associated directly with the API Gateway stage blocks IPs that send too many requests (HTTP floods), with minimal operational overhead. Caching with CloudFront or custom Lambda@Edge blocking is more complex, and CloudWatch only alerts.

DynamoDB Streams captures item changes asynchronously with no impact on the table's performance, and a trigger can publish to a single SNS topic that all four teams subscribe to, with minimal operational overhead. Modifying the application, transactions, or cron scans add load or work.
